newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Consortium says Brisbane airport right for Asia.
newsitem.headline: Consortium says Brisbane airport right for Asia.

text.p: The international consortium which on Wednesday won the right to buy Brisbane airport from the Australian government said the airport was "ideally positioned to capture fast-growing Asia-Pacific air traffic".

The Brisbane Airport Corporation Ltd (BACL) said it was delighted to have won the bid because it represented a unique opportunity to develop a world-class airport facility with high regional growth potential.
"Nowhere else in the world is a high-class, fully operating facility with high growth potential available for sale," said BACL director Koen Rooljmans in a statement.
"Brisbane is ideally positioned to capture the fast-growing Asia-Pacific air traffic and operates within Australia's stable regulatory environment," he added.
The BACL consortium is headed by Amsterdam's Schiphol airport, owned by the Dutch government, and the Commonwealth Bank of Australia.
Other partners include the Port of Brisbane Corporation, and Brisbane City Council.

BACL said the price it paid for the airport, A$1.387 billion, was "based on the airport's solid traffic growth, strong and growing retail income, a well-planned capital expenditure program built around quality, new terminals and the world's best operating practices of Schiphol".

"The BACL consortium represents an excellent team to maximise the potential strengths of Brisbane airport into the next century and develop the airport as the economic engine for Queensland's local and regional economy," it added.
Rooljmans said: "BACL's short to medium term plans for the airport including focusing on airline customers, local stakeholders and developing new and innovative retail strategies.
"In addition we plan to continue major investment on capital works including runway, taxiway, apron and terminal expansion."
Philip Graham, vice-president CBA corporate finance, said: "The finance the plan utilises a multi-layered debt and equity financing package structured and arranged by CBA.
"This package consists of senior bank debt, subordinated bonds which are at the forefront of the mezzanine funds market, and stapled equity.

"Interest rates have been managed via a structure interest rate swap. The innovative structure demonstrates the further development of the bank and institutional investor market for highly-tailored infrastructure projects," he said.
